The Quorum Pact.name: The Quorum Pact
The Quorum Pact.tending: Restraint written as conditional on a quorum of the rivals takes hold all at once once the quorum is reached: West Basin's pumpers signed a contract that bound no one until 80% of rights had signed, and when 82.5% signed the water levels rose; a cooperating fraction can hold off a breakdown even while the rest ride free.
The Quorum Pact.fraying: Each rival seen or heard taking moves the next restrainer past his line: the homeowner who hears his neighbours' sprinklers in the dark turns on his own, 'making the violation unanimous', and a few who send weak workers to the labour day make the rest feel like suckers until only children and old people are sent.
The Quorum Pact.note: Parsimony against The Contingent Commitment: this is restraint before any watch exists (the contract binds at a counted quorum); the watermaster came after.
The Quorum Pact.push: Offer restraint in a race as a contract that binds each signer only once a stated share of the rivals has signed, and count the signatures; do not ask for unilateral restraint (a gift to the rivals) or wait for a monitoring regime to exist first. Expect the holdouts' part of the resource to stay in the race (Hawthorne's trough). The Pumping Race alone says the users can bargain; Tipping alone says each has a cross-over; only the composition says the bargain must carry its own quorum trigger. It differs from The Contingent Commitment (Mutual Monitoring + Tipping), where contingent compliance is sustained by information from ongoing monitoring; here the quorum contract is the way out of the race before any monitoring exists (the watermaster was appointed after the signatures).
The Quorum Pact.reason: No sourced composition. Its conditional-commitment clause is Critical Mass's own threshold run (Ostrom's West Basin signers), and a contract clause is a practice (rule 13); no legal slot joins it to The Shared Pot.

The Fraying passage is Schelling's neighbourhood decline, which is Critical Mass run downward and is not linked in the text to any centre. The figure's own element, the centre's pull being the margin's drain, would need two interlocking runs (for example Critical Mass + Critical Mass, or Flywheel + First-Arriver Lock-In via the Spark), and no source states both. Neither half alone is new, so there is no merge: it stands unseated. Breaks: The Catchment, The Accelerant (and 'Loved to Death', named in out_dyads but not in work.json).

Gaming the Terms + Credited Result via the Outfall (the rule-maker judges by what reaches him) is the nearest legal reading, with 0 arrivals. Not one mechanism with Gaming the Terms (the war-declaring politicians do not beat any rule), so it is unseated rather than merged. Breaks: Proxy Detachment, The Slow Hand, then World-tier Second Nature.

Over the Hump.name: Over the Hump
Over the Hump.tending: A contracted coalition big enough to pass the intersection 'can induce everybody else to shift'. The restraint that began as a bargain becomes the choice each prefers on his own, and the pact's enforcement can be retired.
Over the Hump.fraying: The coalition is viable but short of the intersection: 'a coalition can occur that is insufficient to induce the remainder to choose Right, yet is viable.' Where the pact's own restraint raises the payoff to staying out ('The more the rest of you restrict your whaling, the more whales I catch by staying out'), the chain runs away from the pact. The holdouts relax and 'leave their lights on'. Hawthorne 'saved at least $100,000' pumping over its allotment while its costs 'were spread generally among all signatories', and 'the attempts to reach an agreement with Hawthorne were unsuccessful'. The signers carry the whole load under contract indefinitely.
Over the Hump.push: Size the pact to the intersection, not merely to the number that makes it viable, and first find out whether the restrained choice's payoff rises or falls as more restrain. If it rises (the curves cross), a quorum big enough to pass the crossing tips the rest in and then holds without enforcement. If it falls (each restrainer makes staying out more profitable, as with whaling), no quorum ever self-sustains, and the contract and its enforcement must be permanent, with holdouts expected. The Quorum Pact alone says to make restraint conditional on a counted quorum. The Chain Reaction alone says a few fixed actors can tip conditional ones. Only the composition says which quorum to aim at and whether the pact can later be let go. It differs from The Visible Few (Chain Reaction + Social Tipping Point), where visible costly acts and reported counts make the next act cheaper in a norm with no race or contract. It differs from Critical Mass (tier 2), which has no bargain to reach the hump. It differs from The Shared Pot and Policy Resistance, which have no threshold.

The Standing Account.name: The Standing Account
The Standing Account.tending: In the building phase, flows and stocks rise together: high savings, rising incomes, investments still paying off. A flow account then honestly reports what is being built.
The Standing Account.fraying: The account counts flows, not stocks. Spending and throughput stay strong while the balance sheet and the resource run down, so the civilisation reads itself as rich into the stage where it is already poorer, and keeps drawing down to keep the number up.
The Standing Account.push: When the flow reading is strongest, check the stock (the balance sheet or the resource). A strong flow over a shrinking stock is a sign of Stage 4 (Dalio's 'poorer and still think of themselves as rich'), not a sign of health.
The Standing Account.reason: Both parents are gone: Proxy Detachment merges into The Captured Measure, and The Long Cycle is unseated, so no World slot and no Culture pair remains. Second Nature.name: Second Nature
Second Nature.tending: A shared measure goes without saying, so a whole society can build on it without restating it, and its houses, cities and institutions take the shape of the idea.
Second Nature.fraying: The measure's verdict is taken as a fact about people ('people who are paid less are literally worth less'), and a game rigged by design is rationalised as fair, even by those who lose it: 'that's just the way things are.'
Second Nature.push: Treat it as a paradigm, not an opponent. First show it was made: name the measure, keep pointing at its anomalies, and show it is not obvious to other cultures. Work with the open-minded middle rather than fighting the defenders, because a paradigm can drop 'in a click' while an interest has to be beaten.
Second Nature.reason: Both parents are gone: Proxy Detachment merges into The Captured Measure (a Dyad), and The Slow Hand merges into The Standing Script (a Skein). The sources' two halves are the two legs of The Standing Script. Meadows gives the arranger's leg: an idea sets the structure. Chater gives both the design and the occupants reading its effects as desert. The Set Course.name: The Set Course
The Set Course.tending: The order the winners set up is kept in place long enough for a long building phase. Handled well, with strong human capital maintained, the cycle runs for many generations.
The Set Course.fraying: The arrangement outlives its fundamentals because it is entrenched in how things are done and defended by those it made rich. The delay lets debt and wealth gaps pile up, so when the fall comes it is abrupt.
The Set Course.note: Kept on the parsimony test: lock-in is what carries the cycle past its threshold (Dalio).
The Set Course.push: Judge an entrenched order by the stage of the cycle, read from conditions (debt, gaps, fundamentals), and not by how prominent the order still is. Prominence lags fundamentals, so the most entrenched arrangement looks safest just before it drops.
The Set Course.reason: No sourced composition. Its two halves are separate mechanisms — entrenchment (The Slow Hand) and debt overshoot (the unseated Long Cycle) — and no source joins them.

Adaptation Neglect.reason: Mechanism the sources describe: the judge (an observer, or one's own forecasting self) is asked how a life with a condition goes and answers with the moment the question calls up (Easier Door: substitution), attending to the condition so it looms (Gardener); the person living it has meanwhile withdrawn attention from it (adaptation). The written composition Gardener + Tide has no interlock in any source: the liver's return and the judge's attention never feed each other (the judge does not see the return), so it is parallel at best (rule 3). Kahneman files the case under the focusing illusion in so many words ('and of course in the focusing illusion'; 'wrong ... about the happiness of others'), and The Focusing Illusion (Easier Door + Gardener, C=1 Kahneman) is exactly that substitution-plus-attention mechanism. Chater (495866) arrives at the same observer error independently in text, but both he and Kahneman cite Loewenstein & Ubel (2008), so it counts once. Reader 3's Learning Gradient + Gardener has no source for the interlock. Rule 11: same mechanism, merge; The Focusing Illusion keeps its name.
Adaptation Neglect.name: Adaptation Neglect
Adaptation Neglect.tending: Sustained attention is what care and advocacy are made of
Adaptation Neglect.fraying: A condition they adapted to stays vivid to you forever
Adaptation Neglect.push: To judge how bad a condition is for the person living with it, ask how much of their day they spend attending to it, not how vivid it is to you: 'Adaptation to a new situation, whether good or bad, consists in large part of thinking less and less about it.' The Gardener alone says repeated attention grows a thing; the Tide alone says a state returns to its setpoint. Only the pair says the observer's attention keeps alive what the person living it has already returned from.

The Loud Sample.reason: Mechanism the sources describe: a vocal few speak to move the designers (Namer: saying it loudly so a rollback follows); the designers judge how common a problem or view is by how much of it reaches them (Nearest Light); the change the designers make is what the vocal few answer, and their volume is what the designers weigh (Sellers: a change makes them 'very loud', which can 'override' behavioural data). That is The Agenda's interlock (namers set the ranking by setting the frequency; the rankers' response is what the namers speak to), read at community scale (rule 4). Hopson and Sellers arrive at it independently (no path between them). No source composes Filling the Gap + The Cascade: no passage has an assumption kept against perception, and none has hearers' concern feeding new coverage feeding concern (Sellers' 'echo chamber' is volume, not a self-sustaining chain; Kahneman's cascade is already The Cascade's own C). Reader 2's alternatives (Cascade + Reading the Room, Agenda + Reading the Room) have no arrival. Adversarial check against merging: The Loud Sample's poles talk of representativeness, The Agenda's of importance; both are 'judged prevalence set by frequency of naming', so they are one mechanism and The Agenda keeps its name.
The Loud Sample.name: The Loud Sample
The Loud Sample.tending: When the visible members are representative, availability is an efficient way to know a group
The Loud Sample.fraying: The most extreme voices are amplified into the whole sample, and because everyone hears the same voices, everyone is wrong the same way.
The Loud Sample.push: Treat what the loudest members say as a lead to investigate with a sample you draw yourself, not as the group's view, since everyone else is hearing the same voices (Hopson: use the noise 'as inspiration for more objective research projects'). Filling the Gap alone says assumptions outlast perception; The Cascade alone says a salient event inflates; only the pair says everyone fills the same gap from the same few, so more listening only deepens the shared error.

The Narrow Ledger.reason: Mechanism (Kahneman reporting Thaler): each of 25 division heads judges his own gamble against his own reference, loss averse, one gamble at a time (narrow frame). That is The Mark: judging against a reference point, and Kahneman's reference-dependence passage is The Mark's own C. The heads do not interlock with one another or with the CEO: Kahneman gives 25 parallel runs ('loss averse in his or her domain'), and parallel runs compose nothing (rule 3). The organisation's timidity is their aggregate, a Third Thing, and the CEO's broad frame is a remedy, a push (rule 6), not a run. So the figure is The Mark read at organisation scale (rule 4). The old composition The Tested Price + The Anchor has no named number tested or anchored. Reader 2's Dual Entitlement ×2 (via the owner's reference) has no passage in which the owner's reference acts on the heads. Kahneman's agency remark (KAHN 745883, 'mental self-dealing ... conflicts of interest when the individual acts as an agent') names a conflict but no interlock, so it is a lead only. Merge, not unseat, because the mechanism is sourced; it simply is The Mark.
The Narrow Ledger.name: The Narrow Ledger
The Narrow Ledger.tending: Each division head judges a gamble against his own division's reference and refuses the marginal ones, so loss aversion checks overconfident optimism.
The Narrow Ledger.fraying: Locally prudent refusals sum to an organisation more timid than its owners want
The Narrow Ledger.push: Set a risk policy above the divisions: let the level that sees all the gambles (the CEO's broad frame) decide which to take as a bundle, rather than letting each loss-averse manager price his own. The Tested Price alone says test a named number before accepting it; The Anchor alone says the first number governs; only the pair says each manager's own reference is the anchor, so the correction is to change who frames the bet.

The Borrowed Assent.reason: Mechanism (Kahneman, theory-induced blindness): each scholar privately notes the anomaly, does not pursue it, and reads the field's visible acceptance as a verdict ('trusting the community of experts who have accepted it'). That community is made of scholars doing the same, so private doubts never enter the room and the field holds a position its members privately question. That is The Hall of Mirrors (Echo + Reading the Room) read at field scale (rule 4). Its duration over generations is a reading, not a leg. No source composes The Hall of Mirrors + The Imagined Public: nothing has the scholar build a public from the nearest faces, and The Imagined Public has no sourced element (C, T and F all 0). The old T came from Henrich's faith in cultural inheritance, which is vertical copying across generations (The Faithful Chain's mechanism). It is not carried over, since Kahneman's mechanism is peers reading peers. Reader 2's Faithful Chain proposals were considered and rejected for that reason. Held Silence is rejected too: the scholars keep quiet because they infer, not because they fear. Merge: same mechanism, and the World-tier slot stays empty.
The Borrowed Assent.name: The Borrowed Assent
The Borrowed Assent.tending: Each cohort takes the framework on the assumption that the field has checked it, and so can spend its own effort at the frontier.
The Borrowed Assent.fraying: Everyone assumes someone else verified the foundation; no one did, and a founding flaw stays invisible for generations.
The Borrowed Assent.push: When an observation does not fit the framework everyone uses, pursue it rather than assume someone has already explained it, and ask who in the field actually checked the foundation. The Hall of Mirrors alone says collect private views before the room forms; The Imagined Public alone says test your picture against people outside your circle; only the pair says the 'community of experts' you defer to is itself deferring, so the benefit of the doubt has no one behind it.

The Common Stag.reason: The assurance mechanism the figure is built on is placed by its own T source at another composition. The Common Stag's T quote (OSTROM 273243, Ostrom reporting Levi) is the start of Ostrom's argument that 'the compliance of each depends on the compliance of the others', and Ostrom then says how assurance is produced: 'CPR appropriators create their own internal enforcement to ... assure quasi-voluntary compliers that others also comply', i.e. contingent self-commitment kept going by mutual monitoring. That is The Contingent Commitment (Mutual Monitoring + Mutual Monitoring via The Gardener), sourced to the same Ostrom chapter. Berns' stag hunt (strategic uncertainty: 'each individual has to trust that the other will do the right thing') is the same assurance problem with no composition of its own; Schelling's 'willing to do their part as long as everybody else does' is already The Contingent Commitment's F. One mechanism (conditional cooperation that holds only on visible evidence that others hold), so merge (rule 11). Neither is a book original; the name The Contingent Commitment is kept, with The Common Stag as alias. Berns 214062 adds an independent T and Berns 216509/216744 an independent F to the target.
The Common Stag.name: The Common Stag
The Common Stag.tending: The parties name common rules and arrange each other's conditions so that the cooperative act is safe for everyone at once.
The Common Stag.fraying: Without assurance that others will hold, each takes the safe hare, and the stag nobody could take alone is never hunted.
The Common Stag.push: Before asking anyone to act, give each party visible evidence that the others are holding the rule, because a named rule without that assurance still leaves the safe hare as each one's best move (Ostrom reporting Levi: they comply 'as long as they are confident that others are cooperating'; Berns: 'each individual has to trust that the other will do the right thing'). The Held Commitment alone says someone else holds the conditions, The Arrangement alone says two shape each other's conditions; only the pair says the held rule works only when each can see it held by all.

The Crowded Door.reason: Kahneman gives the mechanism and its parts. Each entrant attends to what it knows best ('entrepreneurs naturally focus on what they know best—their plans and actions'; 'If you only think about your own business'): The Gardener. It answers the easier question ('a difficult question has again been replaced by an easier one'; 'refers to knowledge that is most easily available to them'): The Easier Door. He names the two processes himself: 'WYSIATI and substitution produce both competition neglect and the above-average effect'. The entrants do not interlock: 'you don't think that everybody else is thinking the same way'. They run the same rule side by side, and the overshoot is their sum, which rule 3 says composes nothing. Coaching the Ghost (dwelling on an absent party) is the reverse of competition neglect (ignoring the absent rivals), so it is no part. By rule 4 the market-scale overshoot is the figure its composition gives, read at that scale: The Focusing Illusion (Easier Door + Gardener), whose C is Kahneman's 'substitutes a small part of it for the whole of it'. The optimistic martyrs (failed entrants signalling markets to better-qualified successors) are a one-way transmission edge, not a loop. Marks for the target: C stays 1 (Kahneman again). T gains a candidate: KAHN 571010, 'the effect on the economy as a whole could well be positive', the entrant's narrow focus producing a public good. That would take T from 0 to 1; accept it only if a market-scale Tending is admitted for a Dyad. F stays 1 (KAHN 570900 'excess entry', to be moved onto the target's F).
The Crowded Door.name: The Crowded Door
The Crowded Door.tending: Entrants make more attempts than a cold count would license, and those who fail mark new ground for better-qualified successors.
The Crowded Door.fraying: Each answers the easy question and agrees with every rival, so entry overshoots
The Crowded Door.push: Before entering, answer the question the entrants skipped, 'considering what others will do, how many will come?', and count the rivals entering on the same reasoning; if you back entrants, expect the typical one to lose even when the field as a whole gains. The Focusing Illusion alone says what you attend to looms large; Coaching the Ghost alone says the absent party's question displaces your own; only the pair says every entrant makes the same swap at once, so entry overshoots.

The Disengagement Divide.reason: Gneezy gives the mechanism with two legs, and neither is The Norm Cascade. The leader names the value ('emphasize the importance of team effort', a Namer run) and sets the conditions ('set individual incentives', a Riverbed run), and people follow the conditions: 'Do they follow the talking points or the money? They follow the money.' The T case has the same shape (Branson's risk-taking spread 'top-down' because failure was not punished: 'Don't tell your team to take risks and then punish them for failure'). What spreads is what the conditions pay for, not what saying recruits, so no source supplies the Norm Cascade leg. Brown's divide ('leaders not living by the same values they're preaching') is the same gap between the named word and the held conditions. Namer + Riverbed is The Held Commitment's slot: a declaration holds only while someone holds the conditions for it. Clear and Gneezy's habit contracts are the aligned direction and the mixed signal is the opposed direction: one structure in two directions (rule 6), so merge. Neither figure is a book original; The Held Commitment keeps its name, with The Disengagement Divide as alias. Target marks after the merge: C 2 (Clear; Gneezy), T 2 (Clear; Gneezy), F 2 (Gneezy; Brown). F counts Brown only if a leader's practiced conduct is accepted as the held condition. If not, F stays 1.
The Disengagement Divide.name: The Disengagement Divide
The Disengagement Divide.tending: Those who name a value also hold the conditions that reward it, so each adopter who says it aloud recruits the next and the value spreads as a practised norm.
The Disengagement Divide.fraying: Leaders name the value while arranging conditions that reward its opposite, and people follow what the conditions pay for.
The Disengagement Divide.push: When you name a value, check what the conditions pay for, because people follow the money over the talking points, and put the incentive where the word is (Gneezy: 'Do they follow the talking points or the money? They follow the money'; 'When you want to encourage teamwork, you need to use team incentives'). The Held Commitment alone says a declaration holds when someone holds the conditions, The Norm Cascade alone says saying recruits; only the pair says naming spreads whatever the conditions reward, so a contradicted value spreads the gap.

The Personal Share.reason: Every sourced element of The Personal Share is the personal-to-structural spillover, and both sources treat that spillover as one structure running two ways, crowd out or crowd in. Brownstein: 'personal behavior changes don't necessarily crowd out actions focused on structural change. They can crowd them in too.' Chater & Loewenstein: 'when the carbon tax was framed as costly to individuals, the authors observed crowding out'. The share is cut and handed out by a placer ('corporate campaigns against littering and for carbon footprint monitoring ... to keep the public complacent and distracted'). That is Crowd-Out (Riverbed + Salve): a placed fix whose relief spends the demand for the rule. By rule 6 its two directions are its poles, so Brownstein's crowd-in fills Crowd-Out's empty Tending. The book's assurance clause (shares carried out of sight never add up to the assurance a rule needs) has no source. It is also the mechanism of The Contingent Commitment, where The Common Stag goes, so it adds no third mechanism. Both parents move (The Two Hands) or merge (The Common Stag), so the old composition cannot stand in any case. Target marks: C 1 (Chater), T 0 to 1 (Brownstein 196059), F 1 to 2 (Chater; Brownstein 35274, a separate study). CHATER 76362 (the Sparkman title) is not T: Chater cites it in order to dispute it.
The Personal Share.name: The Personal Share
The Personal Share.tending: The commons cut into a share each person can carry, and the doing builds the constituency
The Personal Share.fraying: Each carries a personal share privately and out of sight, so no one sees the others carrying theirs; the shares never add up to the assurance that would make the rule winnable, and people who frame the problem as their own consumer choices lose the will for anything else ('framing solutions in terms of individual consumer choices decreases people's willingness to take other forms of action').
The Personal Share.push: When you ask people for a personal share, make the shares visible and count them toward the rule change, and distrust a share framing issued by the party that profits from the rule (Brownstein: 'small personal steps can springboard people into backing substantive structural change'; consumer-choice framing 'decreases people's willingness to take other forms of action'). The Common Stag alone says assurance lets people take the stag, The Two Hands alone says the personal fix can occupy the rule change's ground; only the pair says a share carried privately cannot supply the assurance.
